A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Diff-Instruct* work despite the changed title and format. Text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. V2 ends with references; v3 adds readable Appendices A–C.

before.justification: V2 reports original model evaluations on Parti, COCO and HPS benchmarks, including reward/guidance ablations and generated-image comparisons.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds evaluations using a DPO-aligned reference diffusion model.

M1.justification: The generator architecture, DMD2 initialization, score-based objective, alternating updates, pseudo-Huber distance and two CFG approaches are retained. The new reference-checkpoint experiment uses the existing procedure; expanded pseudocode does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use LAION-AESTHETIC training prompts and evaluate on Parti, COCO and the four-style HPS benchmark. The additional reference-model configuration retains this coverage. Conflicting COCO year labels do not establish a newly evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain SDXL, SDXL-DPO, SD3.5-large, FLUX-dev, DMD2, Diff-Instruct, SIM and Diff-Instruct++. The added DI*-SDXL-DPO/DDPO rows represent a proposed-method configuration, not an added external baseline. MaPO is cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5 changes the stated training prompt count from 3 million to 2.2 million under the same aesthetic threshold. V3 also evaluates a DPO-aligned reference checkpoint. COCO-2014/2017 and HPSv2.0/v2.1 labels remain inconsistent, preventing identification of any actual benchmark-protocol switch; the PDFs do not establish rerunning retained results.

E4.justification: V3 adds a reference-model ablation in Section 5.1 and Tables 1 and 3, testing compatibility with pre-aligned SDXL diffusion weights. The existing reward-scale and CFG ablations in Table 2 and the qualitative comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The additional result rows retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All existing numerical rows in Tables 1–3 are retained. V3 adds DPO-reference results, including Parti ImageReward 1.210 and PickScore 0.2342, COCO FID 22.12, and average HPSv2.1 32.26. These are additional configuration results, not corrected scores or same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: V2 states Theorems 3.1 and 3.2 without proofs. V3 adds Appendix A with their derivations, including the score-projection identity and its proof as Theorem A.1. This substantially expands the formal reasoning while retaining the main definitions and theorem statements.

C1.justification: The central claims remain image-data-free preference alignment using score-based regularization, two CFG integration approaches, and a 2.6B one-step model outperforming FLUX-dev on specified preference metrics with 1.88% of its inference time. The post-training framing and new title emphasize claims already present in v2.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the new reference-model experiment as evidence of compatibility and robustness. Its conclusion newly attributes face/hand failures to single-pass generation and proposes few-step extensions. Appendix B adds qualifications about excessive reward strength, diversity and interactions between reward and CFG scales.

D1.justification: Appendices B and C add weighting recommendations, evaluation instructions and illustrative PyTorch pseudocode with optimizer and noise-sampling details. These are additional disclosures, not established changes to existing runs. Conversely, the four comparison prompts in v2's Figure 3 caption disappear despite v3's Figure 2 referring to an appendix prompt list. The model-access link is retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds MaPO (Hong et al., 2024) to the preference-alignment discussion and adds references for Adam and COCO. Its positioning relative to Diff-Instruct++, SIM and diffusion distillation remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 retitles the paper, substantially rewrites the abstract and introduction around post-training and the small-versus-large comparison, and revises the results and conclusion prose. The main algorithm is rewritten into numbered operational steps, with additional appendix organization and renamed method subsections.

P2.justification: The single-column technical report becomes an ICML-style document with two-column main text. The same four figures are resized and relocated; the workflow and visual ablation move to the appendix. Algorithm displays are reorganized, Tables 1 and 3 gain configuration rows, and captions are revised.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the method more assessable through derivations absent from v2, clearer algorithm steps and a useful reference-model ablation. The gain is limited: the new CFG proof has a sign mismatch between Equations A.13 and A.14, Listing 1 contains undefined variables, and protocol labels and prompt documentation are inconsistent. These shortcomings prevent the added material from constituting a substantial overall improvement.
